The gSASRec theorem explicitly assumes uniform negative draws **with replacement** and counts every draw in the loss, including duplicates. Thus α=K/N is expected negative multiplicity per eligible item, not probability of appearing at least once. For 16 draws, these quantities are 16/N and 1−(1−1/N)^16 respectively; the latter applies if duplicates are removed and each distinct negative contributes once. The theorem gives σ(sᵢ)=βP(i)/[βP(i)+α(1−P(i))]; β=α yields calibration under its sampling and expected-loss optimization assumptions. [Original paper, Theorem 5.1](https://eprints.gla.ac.uk/301348/3/301348.pdf)

For history exclusions, the following is a derivation rather than a guarantee established by the paper: conditional on context h and positive y, uniform sampling from eligible set E(h,y) gives expected negative count K·1[i∈E(h,y)]/|E(h,y)|. Averaging over y gives negative weight wᵢ(h); the unrestricted pointwise optimum becomes βP(i|h)/[βP(i|h)+wᵢ(h)]. Substituting αₕ=K/Nₕ recovers the paper’s calibration argument only when wᵢ(h)=αₕ[1−P(i|h)] over the intended prediction universe. Consequently, varying eligible sizes require context-specific accounting, and excluding historical items changes support; replacing the denominator alone does not establish full-catalog calibration.

Implementation implication: retaining duplicate loss terms justifies draw-count K, while deduplicating requires inclusion probabilities. Also preserve relative loss scaling: averaging negatives alone divides their expected weight by K. The authors use β=1−t+tα, with t=1 targeting theoretical calibration and t=0 recovering BCE; their implementation uses α=K/(|I|−1). [Official implementation](https://github.com/asash/gsasrec)
